title: Plate-Loaded Chest-Supported Row
summary: A plate-loaded chest-supported row with a long lever, which loads hardest near full contraction and suits heavy upper-back work.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for upper back (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.7 for lats (helper): each working set adds 0.7 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.65 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.65 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.6 for rear delts (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.
Library rating 0.45 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.45 of a set to the weekly biceps total.

setup.text: Set the chest pad so you can reach the handles with straight arms.
Row the handles back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.

form_cues.cue: Keep your chest on the pad
Pause at the top for a second. The lever makes that position hardest.

mistakes.text: Lifting off the pad to jerk the weight.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, Less upper-back focus.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stable, Lower loading potential, More technical.
Swap sheet: Steadier cable tension, Wider grip.
